title: Minimum Distance Summaries for Robust Neural Posterior Estimation
claim: Adapting the summary at test time by aligning predictive and contaminated data recovers the clean summary and true parameters despite contamination.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: data space, summary space, parameter space; shared color coding
description: Three side-by-side plots with the same color code (red for contaminated or unadapted, green for adapted MDS, dashed purple for observed data). Left: 1D density plot over x. The contaminated observations x̃ (dashed purple) show a main mode near 0 and a small outlier bump near 8–10. The decoder q_ω(x|s̃) (red) is pulled toward the data, while q_ω(x|s*) (green) fits the clean bulk. Middle: 2D contour plot in summary space (s1, s2). Blue clean-training and red contaminated-test density contours are overlaid. Markers show s_ref, s̃ and s*, and s* lands on s_ref. Right: joint posterior plot over θ1 and θ2 with marginal densities on top and right. The red posterior from s̃ is biased, while the green posterior from s* sits on the black θ_true dot. The eye goes first to the left density curves, then follows the colors across the panels.
caption: MDS for a bivariate Gaussian model with 20% of observations ˜x1:100 contaminated by a shift of 8 units. sref,˜s, s∗are the oracle (uncontaminated) summary, test observation (contaminated) summary and adapted MDS summary respectively. Left: MDS aligns the decoder model qω with the contaminated observations ˜x using a robust divergence. Middle: MDS is able to recover the oracle summary despite aligning on the data space. Right: MDS robustifies the NPE and the NPE is now able to recover the true parameters.
abstract: Simulation-based inference (SBI) enables amortized Bayesian inference by first training a neural posterior estimator (NPE) on prior-simulator pairs, typically through low-dimensional summary statistics, which can then be cheaply reused for fast inference by querying it on new test observations. Because NPE is estimated under the training data distribution, it is susceptible to misspecification when observations deviate from the training distribution. Many robust SBI approaches address this by modifying NPE training or introducing error models, coupling robustness to the inference network and compromising amortization and modularity. We introduce minimum-distance summaries, a plug-in robust NPE method that adapts queried test-time summaries independently of the pretrained NPE. Leveraging the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) as a distance between observed data and a summary-conditional predictive distribution, the adapted summary inherits strong robustness properties from the MMD. We demonstrate that the algorithm can be implemented efficiently with random Fourier feature approximations, yielding a lightweight, model-free test-time adaptation procedure. We provide theoretical guarantees for the robustness of our algorithm and empirically evaluate it on a range of synthetic and real-world tasks, demonstrating substantial robustness gains with minimal additional overhead.
